core_obligations: A_total is a weak Serre subcategory (proof lines 5457-5464): cartesian O-modules form a weak Serre subcategory by the cited lemma (hypotheses from Remark remark-augmentation-ringed), and since the restrictions g_n^* are exact, the subcategory of cartesian modules whose restrictions lie in A_{K_n} is weak Serre.

a^* : A -> A_total is an equivalence with inverse La_* (lines 5466-5495): La_*a^*F = F by the bounded equivalence; a^*F lies in A_total plainly; conversely for G in A_total, descent-modules writes G = a^*F, and F lies in A - for U in C, the hypercovering's surjectivity (coproduct of h_{U_{0,i}} to the point becomes surjective) produces a covering {U_j -> U} with maps varphi_j : U_j -> U_{0,tau(j)}; G_0 = a_0^*F identifies the restriction of F to C/U_j with the tau(j)th component of G_0, which lies in A_{U_j} by (item-restriction); (item-local) then gives F|_{C/U} in A_U.

The derived equivalence via the criterion (lines 5497-5521): Cohomology on Sites' unbounded equivalence criterion is applied with its five assumptions checked - (1) clear from Remark remark-augmentation-ringed; (2) and (3) are the preceding paragraph; (4) immediate from (item-bounded-dimension); (5) taking B_total = the objects U/U_{n,i} with U in B, with Cov and d inherited from U, verified by the sanity-check lemma and F_n in A_{K_n}.
proof_roadmap: Show A_total is a weak Serre subcategory (cartesian base + exact restrictions).
Prove the abelian-level equivalence a^* : A -> A_total with inverse La_*, the essential image via a covering argument from the hypercovering surjectivity.
Check the five assumptions of the Cohomology-on-Sites unbounded criterion to lift to derived categories.
difficulty_reason: Equivalence theorem (statement 5431-5453, proof 5455-5521): the module-level counterpart of the bounded equivalence, upgraded to unbounded derived categories by explicitly verifying the five assumptions of the Cohomology-on-Sites criterion; the only input needing work (the essential image of a^*) is a complete covering argument through the hypercovering's surjectivity and the restriction/local axioms; no omitted steps. H2: assumption-checking proof on top of two established equivalences.
